subject: Commit velocity roadmap & trial thresholds — MAP draft
messages:
From: Anna Kim <anna.kim@aeromedtech.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@aeromedtech.com>, John Tse <john.tse@aeromedtech.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial MAP ask and trial expectations

Connor —

Thanks for the demo last week. The team is generally positive; before we proceed to a pilot we need a clearer mutual action plan (MAP) that ties evaluation milestones to commercial commitments. Specifically:

- We need explicit monthly token targets during trial and then for the first 6 months of production (TPM targets).
- Acceptance criteria for performance (latency P95 and inference quality checks).
- Pricing tiers and discount triggers tied to commit cadence (what discount at 3/6/12 months).

Can you share a draft MAP that has concrete TPM numbers and a suggested discount ladder? Procurement would like to see that to prepare internal approvals.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Kim
Head of ML Ops
AeroMed Technologies
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Anna Kim <anna.kim@aeromedtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-24T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial MAP ask and trial expectations

Anna —

Appreciate the clarity. I attached a working MAP (AeroMed_MAP_v1.2.pdf) and a throughput projection spreadsheet that lays out suggested TPM targets month-by-month for a 9-month ramp. High level summary below:

- Pilot (months 0–2): 5M tokens/month, validate end-to-end latency P95 < 400ms and two prompt families for quality checks.
- Early production (months 3–5): 15M / 35M / 60M tokens (month 3 -> month 5), automated prefix caching enabled, expected cost per 1k tokens drops ~22% vs pilot due to batching.
- Stable commit (months 6–9): 120M / 150M / 180M tokens with tiered commit discounts kicking in at 100M TPM sustained for a rolling 30-day window.

Proposed discounts: 5% at 50M TPM sustained for 60 days, 10% at 100M TPM sustained for 30 days, 15% for 200M+ sustained with 6-month commitment. All discounts require passing quality regression evals (we'll provide eval harness).

I'll loop in Marissa to coordinate the commercial proposal and Vivek for any enterprise SLA exceptions. Let me know which parts you want tightened up.

—Connor
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Anna Kim <anna.kim@aeromedtech.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commit velocity roadmap & trial thresholds — MAP draft

Anna —

Thanks for the quick review call yesterday. A couple of clarifications from procurement's perspective:

- Procurement asked that billing cadence be monthly but that we allow credits for under-delivery in the pilot window (month 0–2) tied to availability and performance SLAs.
- They also want an explicit clause that discounts are retroactive to the first day of the month in which the threshold is exceeded (common for their accounting).
- For the 10% discount trigger (100M TPM), they want the option to switch to a quarterly true-up if their traffic pattern spikes.

I've attached a draft SLA amendment that includes proposed language around availability, incident response, and retroactive discounting. Connor — can you confirm we can accommodate the retroactive discounting and the monthly billing + quarterly true-up option?

Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Anna Kim <anna.kim@aeromedtech.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commit velocity roadmap & trial thresholds — MAP draft

Marissa / Anna —

Confirming we can:

- Offer monthly billing with a monthly true-up and a quarterly true-up option (for spikes) as a commercial term.
- Apply discounts retroactively to the start of the month when the TPM threshold is first met, provided the quality guardrails (regression evals and latency SLO) remain green. We will include a 30-day measurement window and standard noise thresholds to prevent ping-ponging.

On the SLA amendment: Vivek and Lauren, quick read from you on whether the incident response SLAs and credit calculation match our standard enterprise playbook — if so we'll send an updated doc to AeroMed for legal.

Connor
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Anna Kim <anna.kim@aeromedtech.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commit velocity roadmap & trial thresholds — MAP draft

Anna / team —

Quick confirmation from Product & Sales Ops: the measurement windows and thresholds Connor proposed are operationally sound. Two operational notes before we finalize:

1) TPM counting: we will publish a token-reporting endpoint and a monthly CSV export for reconciliation. The token-count definition will match the API billing event (post-normalization).
2) Automatic fallback policy: if your production traffic exceeds the committed tier and we cannot immediately provision extra capacity, we will failover to a compatible lower-cost variant for up to 24 hours and notify your on-call — this behavior is included to protect availability.

Next steps: Connor/Marissa to publish MAP v1.3 (incorporate retroactive discount language + billing cadence), then legal exchange with AeroMed. If agreeable, Anna, please confirm and I will share the token-report spec and onboarding checklist.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: AeroMed_MAP_v1.2.pdf (draft MAP), throughput-projection-TPM.xlsx (month-by-month TPM), draft-sla-amendment.docx
